summary: Malaysia procures utility solar through Large Scale Solar rounds sold to TNB under 21-year PPAs, and lets companies buy renewable power over the grid through CRESS. Parts of each round are reserved for Bumiputera companies.

access.reason: Large Scale Solar rounds continue. LSS6, opened in July 2026, offers 2,650 MW of solar with 1,250 MW of batteries.

terms.reason: LSS projects sell to TNB under 21-year PPAs as build, own and operate concessions.

ownership.reason: Two LSS6 packages are reserved for Bumiputera companies, and it is unclear whether foreign firms may join them through consortia.

stability.reason: Corporate supply and self-consumption rules were revised several times in 2025 and 2026.

direction.reason: LSS6 opened in July 2026 with 2,650 MW of solar and 1,250 MW of batteries.

access.reason: CRESS lets companies buy from third-party developers over TNB's grid, and self-consumption solar has its own guidelines.

ownership.reason: Foreign participation rules for corporate supply projects were not confirmed, and parts of national solar programmes are reserved for Bumiputera companies.

stability.reason: Corporate supply and self-consumption rules were revised several times in 2025 and 2026.

direction.reason: No further published change after the 2026 scheme updates was found.

events.title: LSS6 opens with 2,650 MW of solar and 1,250 MW of batteries
